components.gap: Source variant narrowed. Huber's example (iii) (printed p.79) states that with t_0 = T_n(x) every observation with |x_i - t_0| > k may be replaced by the nearer of t_0 - k, t_0 + k without changing the estimate T_n(x), and that t_0 is the mean of the modified sample. The entry (body 145-147) says only that, for any zero t_0, the score still vanishes at t_0 and t_0 is the modified mean; the annex (188-194) proves only that a minimizing location is preserved and states that the replacement need not preserve every tie-breaking rule for every modified sample. The invariance of the estimate itself (the modified sample's zero set is the single point t_0, so its midpoint estimate equals T_{n,k}(x)) is neither stated nor proved. The finite computation, the mean identity and both worked samples are otherwise supplied.

components.gap: Source variant narrowed. Huber (Sec. 7, printed p.83) states that the bias bounds are reached whenever H puts all its mass to the right of k + c, or to the left of -k - c. The entry states attainment only by contamination at any M > c_* + k (body 286-287), and the annex proves it only for H = delta_M plus reflection (428-430). Attainment by every contaminant concentrated on [c_* + k, infinity), or its reflection, is neither stated nor proved, although handbook/parts/p15/robustness-and-sensitivity-of-inference-w02b-p15-071.tex lines 114-116 cite this entry for exactly that claim. The exact root equation, explicit m_k, the small-eps expansion, the eps >= 1/2 case and the identification caveat are otherwise supplied.

defect_observations.observation: The disclaimer that the Winsorizing replacement need not preserve every tie-breaking rule obscures a true source claim. When t_0 is the selected estimate, the modified sample lies in [t_0 - k, t_0 + k] with zero mean residual and is not concentrated at a single endpoint, so its score is strictly decreasing through t_0 and its zero set is {t_0}; the estimate is unchanged under any selection. The caveat applies only to an arbitrary zero t_0 that differs from the selected estimate.

Cites thm:p15-huber-asymmetric-bias for attainment when H puts all its mass to the right of k + c_*. That theorem (body 286-287, annex 428-430) states and proves attainment only for point contamination at M > c_* + k, so the cross-reference relies on a claim the cited entry does not make.

The body clause 'If psi is continuous this is the equation sum psi(x_i - t) = 0' (body 41-42) has no written step in the annex. The missing line is that a continuous midpoint derivative of a convex rho forces psi_- = psi_+. It is immediate but not written; this was not charged as a coverage failure.

The source's statement (printed p.75) that the mean (k = infinity) and the median (k = 0) are the limiting cases for eps = 0 and eps = 1 is only partly rendered. The text states and proves eps = 0 optimality of the mean and the k -> 0 median limit with the literal k = 0 correction. It does not state that the normalized k decreases from infinity to 0 as eps increases from 0 to 1 (implicit only in annex 251-254), or that T_{n,k} equals the mean once k exceeds every residual. Not charged.

Unit-level source-extent observation, not charged to a component here. The asymptotic variance of example (iii) (printed p.79) is stated by the source for a general F with E psi = 0, and its denominator F[-k, k] mishandles atoms at the cut points. The handbook states the corrected formula only for F in C_eps. The source's p.75 assertion that the estimator is asymptotically equivalent to Winsorizing is not addressed in this chapter.

The source (printed p.81) says the limit is either normal or a joined pair of half-normals, and that the latter can occur only if F puts mass on the cut points. C014 supplies the sufficiency example only. The no-atom direction for G = Phi appears in w02b-p15-071 part (iii); its note there that atoms at c +/- k give the two-half-normal law overstates the case of equal atoms. Observation only.

The source's Section 2 inequality (1) (printed p.78: V(psi, F) >= 1/I(F) for F with an absolutely continuous density, with equality only for the maximum likelihood score) appears in this chapter only at F_*. Whether another unit carries the general-F form was not verified. Observation only.
